name: Neck pain and stiffness
goal: Ease everyday neck pain and stiffness with regular movement and short desk breaks, then build the deep neck and upper-back strength that keeps it away.
whoFor: People with everyday neck pain and stiffness, often from desk and screen work, with no arm symptoms or only mild ones.
notFor: Neck pain after an accident or fall that hasn't been checked
Pain, tingling or weakness mainly down one arm (see a physio for a nerve-focused plan)
trackedMetric: Neck pain at its worst today (0-10)
painRules: Mild discomfort up to about 3 out of 10 that settles within an hour is OK. Stop any exercise that sends pain or tingling into the arm.
redFlags: Dizziness, blackouts, double vision, or trouble speaking or swallowing
Numbness, tingling or weakness in both arms or in the legs, or clumsy walking
Neck pain after a fall, accident or blow to the head
Fever, feeling very unwell, or unexplained weight loss
A sudden, severe headache unlike any before
Severe pain that's constant, including at night

phases.name: Settle and move
phases.entryCriteria: Neck pain or stiffness, worse with long sitting or screen use.
phases.exitCriteria: Daily pain is mostly 3 out of 10 or less and you can turn your head comfortably.

phases.name: Build strength
phases.entryCriteria: Pain is low and movement is comfortable.
phases.exitCriteria: Little or no pain with work and daily life for 2 weeks. Keep the desk breaks and 2-3 strength sessions a week.

items.note: Start with 5-second holds if 10 seconds is too hard.

references: Blanpied PR, et al. 2017. Neck pain: revision 2017. Clinical practice guidelines. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 47(7):A1-A83.
Jull G, et al. 2002. A randomized controlled trial of exercise and manipulative therapy for cervicogenic headache. Spine 27:1835-43.
